settings_ui_language_desc: Follows the target language by default — the UI speaks the language you read
settings_general_desc: Language pair, default engine, and how translations are presented.
settings_default_provider_desc: Used when a request names no engine
settings_skip_langs_desc: Text detected in these languages is left alone (the target is always skipped)
settings_detector_ready: Ready — non-target languages are skipped before translating
settings_detector_unavailable: Not supported by this browser (falls back to script heuristics plus a post-translation check)
settings_detector_downloadable: A small on-device model enables precise pre-translation skipping
settings_input_desc: Type in any field, then tap the space bar {count} times in a row — what you wrote is translated in place.
settings_input_hint_3: to pick the language for that one rewrite.
settings_input_target_desc: The language you write into — usually the opposite of your reading target
settings_style_desc: How the translation is marked beside the original — it blends in by default. The swatches below are live; click to apply.
provider_section_desc: The built-in free machine translation, plus LLM providers you add (bring your own key).
provider_models_failed: Couldn't fetch the model list — check your network or API key
provider_remove_confirm_text: This removes the engine and its API key.
provider_free_desc: Free, no API key needed. The built-in fallback engine.
provider_base_url_insecure: Use an https:// URL — http:// only works for localhost.
provider_headers_desc: One per line, as Header-Name: value
provider_params_desc: Leave a field empty to use the model's own default. Reasoning models (OpenAI o-series, gpt-5) usually accept only the default temperature.
provider_param_max_tokens_desc: Set too low, this truncates whole-page batch translation.
provider_param_reasoning_desc: Vendors spell extended thinking differently, and Gemini has no off switch at all — there, Off buys its lowest level instead. A model that refuses its family parameter fails at Validate.
provider_validate_hint_model: Set a model, then validate to enable.
site_section_desc: The default behaviour on every site, plus per-site overrides.
backup_section_desc: Export your settings (API keys included) to a JSON file, or restore from one.
backup_reset_confirm_text: This wipes every engine, API key and site rule. Consider exporting first.
backup_imported: Config imported. Every engine came in as a draft — validate the connection to switch it back on.
panel_input_placeholder: Type or paste text to translate…
panel_swap_disabled: Pick a concrete source language to swap
input_failed: Couldn't translate — your draft is untouched
error_no_key: This engine is missing an API key. Please add one in settings.
error_timeout: The engine took too long to respond. Please try again later.
error_interrupted: Translation interrupted. A retry usually fixes this.
error_network: Network connection failed. Please check your connection and retry.
error_rate_limited: Too many requests. Please wait a moment and try again.
error_unavailable: The translation service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again.
styles_section_desc: Shape tone, register, and word choice with natural language — the active style applies to page, selection, and input translation alike.
style_plain_desc: Straight translation with no style directives (default).
style_builtin_colloquial_desc: Natural spoken phrasing, short rhythms, no stiff literalism.
style_builtin_academic_desc: Formal register, precise terminology, hedged claims preserved.
style_builtin_technical_desc: API names stay untranslated, imperative mood, consistent terminology.
style_builtin_literary_desc: Rhythm and imagery first, freer word order, the original voice preserved.
styles_directives_hint: Describe the tone and wording you want in natural language; English works best. Taste only — the engine guards the output format.
styles_preview_label: Assembled preview (the system prompt actually sent)
expert_desc: Take over the whole prompt template (e.g. to add few-shot examples). When set, that pipeline no longer injects the translation style.
expert_batch_system_label: Whole-page batch · system template (must keep the [[{salt}#N]] marker instruction)
expert_placeholders_hint: Placeholders: {target} target language · {source} source language · {title} page title · {text} the text (user template only) · {salt} batch marker salt (batch template only)
expert_error_batch_marker: The batch template must keep the literal fragment [[{salt}# — whole-page translation depends on this marker instruction; removing it breaks it outright.
expert_error_single_text: The user template must contain {text}, or the text to translate is never sent at all.
styles_rules_desc: Pin a style to matching sites; the longest matching pattern wins, otherwise the global default applies.
glossary_section_desc: Pin exact translations for terms. Injected on demand: an entry only enters the prompt when its term occurs in the text — a large glossary costs nothing extra. Optional site scope, same matching as site rules.
glossary_import_err_empty: No usable term rows in the file — it needs source/target columns (CSV/TSV) or the matching JSON fields.
glossary_import_err_unrecognized: Could not parse the file — supported: an exported JSON set, or CSV/TSV rows of source,target[,note].
settings_page_context_desc: Overview the page before translating: names and context stay consistent page-wide. Sends the FULL page text (including parts you never scroll to) to the engine, and costs one extra call per page. AI engines only.
settings_rich_text_desc: Translations keep the original's links, bold and inline code. If format markers confuse an engine and the translation reads stilted, turn this off for cleaner plain-text output.
interleave_desc: Place each translated paragraph right after its source paragraph in multi-paragraph blocks
